route.name: Haifa-Deraa Line
route.notes: Inaugurated 15 Oct 1905; carried ~3/4 of Hejaz traffic despite being ~1/5 of construction.  [route] The full Hejaz branch to the Mediterranean; its western portion is the Jezreel Valley line. The 8 ORIGINAL 1905 stations were Haifa, Balad al-Sheikh, Kfar Yehoshua (Tel Shammam), Afula, Beit She’an, Gesher, Tzemah/Samakh and al-Hamma; the others are LATER halts (several founded after 1905 — e.g. Nesher 1925, Ein Harod 1921, HaSade 1934, Beit Yosef 1937), so treat them as additions, not original stops. Arlosorow Halt (1937) and a temporary 'Jordan Valley' halt (1936) are documented but not placed.  [gorge] The Samakh–Deraa eastern section (73 km, +529 m climb, 8 tunnels ~1,100 m, 329 bridges/aqueducts up the Yarmuk gorge) is well documented as ENGINEERING but its intermediate STATION NAMES are not in the consulted sources — a research gap (the famous Tell esh-Shehab bridge, a T.E. Lawrence target, lies on this stretch; verify).
route.history: The Haifa–Deraa branch of the Hejaz Railway (1,050 mm), inaugurated 15 October 1905, gave the Hejaz system its outlet to the Mediterranean at Haifa. It ran ~161 km up the Jezreel and Harod valleys to the Jordan, then climbed the Yarmuk gorge to meet the Hejaz main line at Deraa.
